attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the causal link. Dropping 'precisely' slightly softens how exclusive the cause is meant to be, but the contract flags this.

contract.note: Reading reliability as a principal cause of uneven commercialization, without requiring that adoption was absent, is fair and ordinary. The two-year window comes from the surrounding text.

evidence.note: BCG survey of 100 information-services professionals, early 2024. Accuracy was the barrier to scaling cited most often. Supports the mechanism, but only in one sector.
McKinsey, early 2024: regular gen-AI use rose sharply. Rising use can coexist with impeded commercialization, so this neither proves nor refutes the cause.

Deloitte, mid-2024: most firms moved few experiments into production, which suggests halting progress. But it names data, risk and governance as barriers and does not isolate unreliability as the cause.

reviews.rationale: There is some evidence of stalled deployment (Deloitte), and accuracy is the top barrier in one sector (BCG). No broad evidence shows unreliability was the principal cause across the market, and none shows commercialization was unhindered or that reliability didn't matter. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A present-tense observation that hallucinations recur. Generalizing to LLMs fits the context, which discusses LLMs broadly.

contract.note: Taking 'regular' to mean recurring rather than most responses is an ordinary, fair reading. The 2024 window fits the post.

evidence.note: SimpleQA, a company paper dated 2024-10-30, within the window. GPT-4o, o1-preview and Claude-3.5-Sonnet answered many questions wrongly, with abstentions counted separately. The questions were adversarially selected, but the result still shows recurring fabrication.

reviews.rationale: A systematic 2024 evaluation with documented methods found repeated incorrect factual answers from widely used models, including another company's model. It is a company disclosure, but it reports failures, which cuts against the company's interest. Nothing in the packet shows hallucinations had become exceptional. The support condition is met.

attribution.note: 'They didn't' is Marcus's own assertion. The projections he attributes to Labenz and investors are framing and are not scored.

semantics.note: A retrospective observation that hallucinations did not soon recede. Elsewhere Marcus concedes they 'may have declined'.

contract.note: The contract flags both the literal ('declined') and loose ('faded to minor') readings of 'recede'. The support condition also requires that rates did not fall, which is strict, so the result turns on the reading.

evidence.note: OpenAI, March 2023: GPT-4 significantly reduced hallucinations compared with GPT-3.5. A company disclosure. It cuts against the literal reading, though OpenAI calls the problem 'still a real issue'.
o1 system card: o1 hallucinates less than GPT-4o, so rates were falling. But rates remain high (0.44 to 0.61 on SimpleQA), which supports persistence. A company disclosure.
Tow Center audit, November 2024: ChatGPT gave wrong or partly wrong answers in 153 of 200 source queries. Fabrication was still common.

reviews.rationale: Holds: hallucinations stayed frequent and did not fade into a minor problem (e2's rates, e3's audit), so the contradiction condition is not met. Fails: OpenAI's own data show measurable declines over 2023–2024, so the support condition's requirement that rates did not fall is not met. Supported on the loose reading, contradicted on the literal one.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the 'despite scaling and RAG' qualifier. 'Tried practically everything' is rhetoric and is correctly left out.

contract.note: Reading 'not gone away' as hallucination rates still clearly above zero is plain and fair. The GPT-4o-era window is reasonable.

evidence.note: o1 system card, published after the post but describing models of the period. Scaled frontier models still show high SimpleQA hallucination rates. A company disclosure, but against interest.
Stanford preregistered study, May 2024: commercial RAG legal tools hallucinated 17–33% of the time.
Tow Center audit, November 2024: ChatGPT Search, which uses retrieval, gave wrong source answers in most of 200 tests.

reviews.rationale: Several evaluations from mid-to-late 2024, including independent ones, show both scaled frontier models and RAG products hallucinating at clearly non-zero rates. No evidence shows near-zero rates. The support condition is met.
